selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main problem being addressed to the lower self in this passage?
questions.answer: It is being corrected for loving praise, fame, and self-importance.

questions.question: What signs of ego are named at the beginning?
questions.answer: Craving honor, fame, praise, and acting as though no one equals it.

questions.question: What do those natural images suggest about visible means?
questions.answer: They are only instruments through which results appear.

questions.question: How does free choice make the lower self more accountable?
questions.answer: It allows the person to respond with gratitude or with arrogance, so misuse becomes blameworthy.

questions.question: Why is claiming ownership of blessings described as wrongful?
questions.answer: Because those gifts come from Allah, so treating them as one’s private property is unjust.

questions.question: Why were the lower self and nature made as veils according to the passage?
questions.answer: So that things whose beauty is not immediately seen could be linked to them, while Allah remains understood as free from fault.

questions.question: How does the passage answer the thought that being chosen to display good works proves personal merit?
questions.answer: It says such gifts may come first to the one who is most needy and poor before Allah, not the most worthy in his own eyes.

questions.question: What reversal happens when the lower self or nature forgets this role?
questions.answer: They start presenting themselves as if they share in divine creativity.

questions.question: Why is being a channel for beauty not the same as being beautiful in oneself?
questions.answer: Because what passes through a person does not become his essential possession.

questions.question: What does the passage encourage a successful person to remember about himself?
questions.answer: He should remember his dependence, weakness, and need for Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What character traits of the lower self are criticized at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: Love of status, desire for fame, hunger for praise, and extreme ego.

questions.question: Why is the lower self said to deserve blame rather than admiration?
questions.answer: Because it damages blessings through pride, ingratitude, and acting as if those gifts belong to it.

questions.question: What mistaken conclusion does the lower self want to draw from blessings?
questions.answer: That it deserves pride and admiration.

questions.question: How does pride affect a blessing spiritually?
questions.answer: It weakens and spoils its true value.

questions.question: What false center of life does the passage reject?
questions.answer: Making the self the main focus.

questions.question: What kind of self-understanding leads to true excellence?
questions.answer: Seeing one’s neediness and recognizing Allah.

questions.question: What judgment is given about worshipping oneself or worshipping nature?
questions.answer: It is deep foolishness and a major wrong.

questions.question: What connection does the opening verse have to the warning given to the lower self?
questions.answer: It warns against rejoicing in what one claims and wanting praise for what one did not truly accomplish.

questions.question: What is wrong with thinking that reflected beauty proves personal greatness?
questions.answer: Reflected beauty may simply pass through a person without becoming his own excellence.

questions.question: What attitude toward one’s own talents best fits this passage?
questions.answer: A servant’s attitude that sees talent as mercy from Allah.

questions.question: What verse is placed before the rebuke to the lower self, and what warning does it give in meaning?
questions.answer: It warns people not to feel secure when they enjoy false credit and seek praise for what is not truly theirs.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the lower self is unlike the seed and the branch in an important way?
questions.answer: Because the lower self has choice, so it can misuse blessings through arrogance and bad response.

questions.question: What qualities are said to suit the lower self better than fame and praise?
questions.answer: Humility, repentance, and seeking forgiveness.

questions.question: What role does human choice play in this rebuke?
questions.answer: Choice makes the self responsible for turning gifts into reasons for arrogance.

title: Title and 1 Point Discipline and Gratitude Lesson for the Commanding Self
